4.1 Sample selection

Table 1 shows our sample selection. We began by considering all 728 companies incorporated in Great Britain that have ordinary stocks listed in the LSE premium category and
tradedontheLSEMainMarket.WemergedthislistofcompanieswiththeThomsonReuters
databases to identify 338 nonfinancial companies with data in Worldscope and Datastream
(i.e.,eliminatingSICcodes6000to6999).Thisselectionwasmadebecausemanybanking,
insurance, trust, and investment companies are traded in the LSE Main Market (KPMG
2014), while our study focuses on nonfinancial companies, as has the literature (e.g.,
CarcelloandLi 2013;Czerneyetal. 2017;Seetharamanetal. 2002). <sup>23</sup> Wereadandmanually
codedinformationfromannualreports(e.g.,auditor’sreportlength,namesofauditfirmand
audit partner, number and description of significant risks of material misstatement in the
auditor’s report, materiality amount, audit fees, and the number and descriptions of significant accounting issues in the audit committee report). Finally, we complemented our data
with financial and market variables from the Thomson Reuters databases (Worldscope,
Fundamentals, and Datastream). We also identified the date on which each company’s
annual report was made available to investors (i.e., the filing date) and the earnings release
date in the LSE RNS and NSM databases. Similar to the sample selection for premium
companies,westartedwith724AIMcompanieslistedintheLSEandincorporatedinGreat
Britain and then excluded financial companies and those without data in Thomson Reuters.

23 Excluding financial firms is a typical practice in audit fees and audit quality research. Banking and other
financial companies (e.g., mutual funds) face high levels of regulatory scrutiny and have additional mandatory
disclosures. There are no straightforward reasons to expect that the expanded auditor’s report will be
incrementally informative for these companies. We reviewed a number of reports for these companies and
found that the most common risk mentioned is valuation of assets, focusing on determining the fair value of
